hero.title: Production-ready Web3: from working demo to calm operations
hero.subtitle: Design environments and control, build a pipeline, write honest wallet messages, monitor what users feel and plan a staged launch and a calm response when something breaks. Every task is checked and explained.

Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.

faq.q: Does the platform run my pipeline or deploy contracts?
faq.a: No. The labs check your plans, calculations and writing. You run the code and pipelines in your own tools, on test networks while learning.

faq.q: Do I need the earlier courses?
faq.a: You should be comfortable with Solidity and Web3 JavaScript, for example from the earlier courses in this series.

faq.q: Will this make my product safe?
faq.a: It teaches the practices that reduce risk. Products holding real value still need independent audits, legal advice and continuing operations.

activities.title: Budget a deployment
activities.objective: Estimate the cost of deploying several contracts with a safety buffer and compare it with a budget.
activities.scenario: A launch deploys 4 contracts at about 1,800,000 gas each. Gas costs 20 gwei and ETH is 250,000 rupees. Add a 25% buffer for price swings. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the total gas.
In B8 convert it to ETH using the gas price in gwei.
In B9 convert it to rupees.
In B10 add the safety buffer percentage.
In B11 show Over budget if B10 is above the budget in B12, otherwise Within budget.

checks.label: B7 is the total gas
B8 is the cost in ETH
checks.explain: Gas times gwei over a billion.

checks.label: B9 is the cost in rupees
B10 is the cost with buffer
B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>B12,"Over budget","Within budget")

activities.title: Score launch readiness
activities.objective: Turn a launch checklist into a weighted score and a clear verdict.
activities.scenario: A team scores five readiness checks by importance. Each check passes (1) or fails (0).
steps: In D2 work out the points for the first check: weight times passed. Fill down to D6.
In B8 add up the points earned.
In B9 add up the weights.
In B10 work out the percentage.
In B11 show Ready to launch for 90 or more, Needs work for 70 or more, otherwise Not ready.

checks.label: D2 is the points
D5 is the points
B8 is the points earned
checks.hint: =SUM(D2:D6)

checks.label: B9 is the points possible
checks.hint: =SUM(B2:B6)

checks.label: B10 is the percentage
B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>=90,"Ready to launch",IF(B10>=70,"Needs work","Not ready"))

activities.title: Spend your error budget
activities.objective: Turn an availability target into allowed downtime and decide how careful to be with releases.
activities.scenario: Your service promises 99.5% availability over a 30-day month. This month there have been 3 incidents averaging 45 minutes. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the minutes in the month (days times 24 times 60).
In B8 work out the allowed downtime in minutes.
In B9 work out the downtime used so far.
In B10 work out the percentage of the budget used.
In B11 show SLO missed above 100, Slow down releases above 75, otherwise Healthy.

checks.label: B7 is the minutes in the month
B8 is the allowed downtime
checks.explain: The share you may be down.

checks.label: B9 is the downtime used
B10 is the budget used
B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>100,"SLO missed",IF(B10>75,"Slow down releases","Healthy"))

activities.title: Final project: write a production readiness review
activities.objective: Produce a professional readiness review for a Web3 product, covering architecture, control, testing, user experience, monitoring, launch and open risks.
activities.scenario: Your team is about to launch a vault product with a front end, an indexer and contracts. Write the review that decides whether to launch.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Production readiness review'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Architecture, Control and governance, Testing and CI, User experience, Monitoring and response, Launch plan, Open risks and decision.
Under Control and governance mention a time-lock, a multi-signature wallet and a ceiling on parameters.
Under Testing and CI list at least four checks in bullets.
Under Monitoring and response mention an alert threshold and a runbook.
Under Open risks and decision give a clear launch, delay or do-not-launch decision with reasons.
Mention that an independent audit is required for real value.
Keep it between 340 and 680 words.
